title: Λέων καὶ δελφίς
part: The Lion and the Dolphin (Chambry 202 · Perry 145)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 202 (= Perry 145). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », [ ] for words Chambry deletes as interpolated). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Λέων ἐπί τινι αἰγιαλῷ πλαζόμενος, ὡς ἐθεάσατο δελφῖνα παρακύψαντα, [ὡς] ἐπὶ συμμαχίαν τοῦτον παρεκάλεσε λέγων ὅτι ἁρμόττει μάλιστα φίλους αὐτοὺς καὶ βοηθοὺς γενέσθαι· ὁ μὲν γὰρ τῶν θαλαττίων ζῴων, αὐτὸς δὲ τῶν χερσαίων βασιλεύει.
sentences.tr: Leōn epi tini aigialōi plazomenos, hōs etheasato delphina parakypsanta, [hōs] epi symmachian touton parekalese legōn hoti harmottei malista philous autous kai boēthous genesthai· ho men gar tōn thalattiōn zōiōn, autos de tōn chersaiōn basileuei.
sentences.l: A lion, roaming on a certain shore, when he saw a dolphin putting his head up, [as] called upon him for an alliance, saying that it is especially fitting that they become friends and helpers; for the one is king of the creatures of the sea, and he himself of those of the dry land.
sentences.i: A lion roaming on a stretch of shore saw a dolphin put his head above the water, and invited him into an alliance, saying that it was altogether fitting that they should become friends and helpers to one another: the dolphin was king of the creatures of the sea, and he himself of those of the dry land.
sentences.n: The second ὡς stands in square brackets: Chambry judges it an interpolated repetition of the ὡς that opens the temporal clause, and deletes it. The bracket is carried across into the romanization and the literal line so the reader can see exactly what the editor has struck. παρακύπτω is to lean forward and put one's head out — from a window, or here from the water. βασιλεύω takes the genitive of what one is king over.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ ἀσμένως ἐπινεύσαντος, ὁ λέων ἐπὶ πολὺν χρόνον μάχην ἔχων πρὸς ταῦρον ἄγριον ἐπεκαλεῖτο τὸν δελφῖνα ἐπὶ βοήθειαν.
sentences.tr: Tou de asmenōs epineusantos, ho leōn epi polyn chronon machēn echōn pros tauron agrion epekaleito ton delphina epi boētheian.
sentences.l: And he having gladly nodded his assent, the lion, having a fight for a long time against a wild bull, called upon the dolphin for help.
sentences.i: When the dolphin had gladly agreed, the lion, long engaged in a fight with a wild bull, called on him for help.
sentences.n: A genitive absolute clears the first scene before the second begins — the fable's standard hinge. ἐπινεύω is to nod toward someone in assent; Greek nods downward for yes and tosses the head back (ἀνανεύω) for no.

sentences.t: Ὡς δὲ ἐκεῖνος καίπερ βουλόμενος ἐκβῆναι τῆς θαλάσσης οὐκ ἠδύνατο, ᾐτιᾶτο αὐτὸν ὁ λέων ὡς προδότην.
sentences.tr: Hōs de ekeinos kaiper boulomenos ekbēnai tēs thalassēs ouk ēdynato, ēitiato auton ho leōn hōs prodotēn.
sentences.l: And when that one, although wishing to, was not able to come out of the sea, the lion blamed him as a traitor.
sentences.n: καίπερ with a participle is the regular concessive: 'although he wished to'. The ὡς of ὡς προδότην gives the lion's own view of the case, not the narrator's.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ ὑποτυχὼν εἶπεν· « Ἀλλὰ μὴ ἐμὲ μέμφου, ἀλλὰ τὴν φύσιν, ἥτις με θαλάττιον ποιήσασα γῆς οὐκ ἐᾷ ἐπιβαίνειν. »
sentences.tr: Ho de hypotychōn eipen· « Alla mē eme memphou, alla tēn physin, hētis me thalattion poiēsasa gēs ouk eāi epibainein. »
sentences.l: And he, taking-up-the-word, said: « But do not blame me, but nature, which, having made me a creature of the sea, does not allow me to set foot on land. »
sentences.n: ὑποτυχών is to catch up the other's words and answer, not to seize anything. μή with the present imperative forbids a thing already under way — 'stop blaming me'. ἐπιβαίνω takes the genitive of what is trodden.

sentences.t: Οὕτως καὶ ἡμᾶς δεῖ φιλίαν σπενδομένους τοιούτους ἐπιλέγεσθαι συμμάχους οἳ ἐν κινδύνοις παρεῖναι ἡμῖν δύνανται.
sentences.tr: Houtōs kai hēmas dei philian spendomenous toioutous epilegesthai symmachous hoi en kindynois pareinai hēmin dynantai.
sentences.l: So too we must, when pouring a libation of friendship, pick out for ourselves such allies as are able to be at our side in dangers.
sentences.i: So too, when we ratify a friendship, we must pick out allies of the sort who can be at our side in danger.
sentences.n: σπένδομαι φιλίαν is to pour the libation that seals an agreement, and so to ratify it — the pact is a religious act before it is anything else. ἐπιλέγομαι in the middle is to choose out for oneself.
